Standard Schedule 1.1 Core hours The standard office schedule is 9:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, with a one-hour meal break. 1.2 Team schedules Teams with operational requirements may use approved schedules different from the standard schedule. 2. Purpose 1.1 Standard The Code of Conduct establishes expected professional behavior and supports a respectful, ethical, and secure workplace. 2. Respectful Workplace 2.1 Respect Employees must communicate professionally and treat colleagues, customers, and partners with dignity. 2.2 Harassment Harassment, bullying, intimidation, and retaliation for raising a good-faith concern are prohibited. 3. Conflicts of Interest 3.1 Disclosure Employees must disclose situations that could reasonably create a conflict between personal interests and company responsibilities. 3.2 Gifts Employees must follow company rules concerning gifts, hospitality, and benefits from customers, vendors, or partners. 4. personal interests and company responsibilities. 3.2 Gifts Employees must follow company rules concerning gifts, hospitality, and benefits from customers, vendors, or partners. 4. Use of Company Resources 5.1 Acceptable use Company devices, accounts, software, and networks must be used responsibly and in accordance with security requirements. 5.2 Records Employees must not knowingly falsify business records, attendance records, expense claims, or other company information. 6. Page 1 NexaCore Technologies COMPENSATION POLICY Version: 2026.1 | Effective Date: January 1, 2026 Document Type: Human Resources Policy | Classification: 1. Purpose 1.1 Objective This policy describes the principles used to administer employee compensation, salary reviews, and selected incentive processes. 2. Salary Structure 2.1 Components Compensation may include base salary and, where applicable, variable or incentive components defined by the employee's role and plan. 2.2 Confidentiality Employees should handle compensation information responsibly and protect confidential payroll information belonging to others. 3. Salary Reviews 3.1 Annual review Eligible employees may participate in an annual compensation review based on performance, market considerations, role scope, and company budget. 3.2 No automatic increase Participation in a review does not guarantee a salary increase.

It should be read together with the detailed policies maintained by Human Resources. 1.2 Scope The handbook applies to regular full-time and part-time employees unless a specific policy or employment agreement states otherwise. Contractors, interns, and temporary workers may be subject to separate terms. 1.3 Policy precedence Where a detailed policy contains a requirement that differs from a general statement in this handbook, the applicable detailed policy takes precedence for that subject.

Page 1 NexaCore Technologies LEAVE POLICY Version: 2026.1 | Effective Date: January 1, 2026 Document Type: Human Resources Policy | Classification: 1. Purpose and Scope 1.1 Purpose This policy defines the leave categories, eligibility, approval process, carry-forward rules, and documentation expectations for NexaCore employees. 1.2 Scope The policy applies to eligible employees unless an employment agreement or applicable law provides a different entitlement. 2. Annual Leave 2.1 Entitlement Eligible full-time employees receive 18 days of annual leave per calendar year. Part-time entitlement may be prorated according to working arrangements. 2.2 Accrual Annual leave is credited through the company's leave administration process. Employees should review their available balance before submitting requests. 2.3 Approval Employees should normally submit planned annual leave at

Accrual Annual leave is credited through the company's leave administration process. Employees should review their available balance before submitting requests. 2.3 Approval Employees should normally submit planned annual leave at least five working days in advance. Approval depends on team coverage and business requirements. 3. Sick Leave 3.1 Use Sick leave may be used for personal illness, medical appointments, or recovery. Employees should notify their manager as soon as reasonably possible. 3.2 Documentation Human Resources or a manager may request supporting documentation where permitted by company rules and applicable law. 4. Casual Leave 4.1 Entitlement Eligible employees receive 6 days of casual leave per calendar year for short-term personal needs. 4.2 Restrictions Casual leave is subject to approval and should

4. Casual Leave 4.1 Entitlement Eligible employees receive 6 days of casual leave per calendar year for short-term personal needs. 4.2 Restrictions Casual leave is subject to approval and should not be used to bypass planned annual-leave procedures. 5. Carry Forward and Expiry

Page 2 5.1 Carry forward Up to 5 unused annual-leave days may be carried into the following calendar year. Carried days must be used by March 31 unless an approved exception applies. 5.2 Non-transferability Leave balances are personal to the employee and cannot be transferred to another employee. 6. Leave Application Process 6.1 Request Employees submit leave through the approved HR system and provide dates, leave category, and required supporting information. 6.2 Manager decision Managers consider staffing, deadlines, and policy eligibility before approving or declining a request. 7. Extended and Special Leave 7.1 Special circumstances Additional leave categories may be available under separate company policies or applicable law. Human Resources should be consulted when a circumstance is not covered here.

Special Leave 7.1 Special circumstances Additional leave categories may be available under separate company policies or applicable law. Page 1 NexaCore Technologies RESIGNATION AND EXIT POLICY Version: 2026.1 | Effective Date: January 1, 2026 Document Type: Human Resources Policy | Classification: 1. Purpose 1.1 Scope This policy describes the process for employee resignation, notice, knowledge transfer, clearance, and access closure. 2. Resignation 2.1 Written notice Employees must submit written resignation through the approved HR process. 2.2 Notice period The standard notice period is 30 calendar days unless the employee's employment agreement specifies otherwise or an approved exception applies. 3. Notice Management 3.1 Handover Employees serving notice must complete reasonable knowledge transfer, documentation, and transition activities. 3.2 Leave during notice Leave during the notice period requires normal approval and may be restricted where operationally necessary. 4. reasonable knowledge transfer, documentation, and transition activities. 3.2 Leave during notice Leave during the notice period requires normal approval and may be restricted where operationally necessary. 4. Company Property 4.1 Return Employees must return laptops, access cards, equipment, documents, and other company property by the required exit date. 4.2 Data Company information must not be copied, retained, or transferred to personal accounts or devices. 5. Access Closure 5.1 Accounts System and application access is disabled according to the company's exit process. 5.2 Security Employees must not attempt to access company systems after access has been revoked. 6. Exceptions 7.1 Management approval Changes to the standard notice process require documented approval from authorized management and Human Resources. Page 1 NexaCore Technologies WORK FROM HOME POLICY Version: 2026.1 | Effective Date: January 1, 2026 Document Type: Human Resources Policy | Classification: 1. Purpose 1.1 Objective The work-from-home program supports flexible work while maintaining productivity, collaboration, information security, and customer service. 2. Eligibility 2.1 Role eligibility Roles may be eligible when duties can be performed effectively away from the office and business coverage can be maintained. 2.2 Performance Employees are expected to meet performance and attendance expectations while working remotely. 3. Remote Work Allowance 3.1 Standard allowance Eligible employees may work remotely up to 2 days per week with manager approval, subject to team schedules and business needs. 3.2 Office requirements Managers may require additional office attendance for collaboration,

may work remotely up to 2 days per week with manager approval, subject to team schedules and business needs. 3.2 Office requirements Managers may require additional office attendance for collaboration, training, customer meetings, or operational needs. 4. Approval Process 4.1 Request Employees submit proposed remote-work days through the approved process or manager workflow. 4.2 Approval Approval is discretionary and may be changed when business conditions require increased on-site presence. 5. Working Hours 5.1 Availability Remote employees must remain available during their agreed working hours and attend required meetings. 5.2 Overtime Remote work does not change overtime or working-time rules applicable to the employee. 6. Security and Equipment

Page 2 6.1 Security Employees must use approved devices and security controls and must not expose company data to unauthorized persons. 6.2 Equipment Company equipment must be maintained securely and returned when requested or when employment ends. 7. Performance and Review 7.1 Review Managers may periodically review remote-work effectiveness based on performance, collaboration, attendance, and business requirements. Purpose This policy defines security requirements for employees who access enterprise systems, applications, or information while working remotely. 2. Device Security Employees must use company-managed devices whenever available. Devices must use screen locking, current security updates, and approved endpoint protection. Employees must not disable security controls. 3. Network Access Remote access to internal systems must use the organization's approved secure access mechanism. Public or unsecured Wi-Fi should not be used for sensitive enterprise information unless an approved secure connection is active. 4.
